expectations.text: SQL injection in login (string-built query)
expectations.evidence: F01: routes/login.ts:33 'interpolates req.body.email into a SQL literal'; result controls account selection/token issuance.

expectations.text: SQL injection in product search
expectations.evidence: F02: routes/search.ts:20-22 inserts q into LIKE expressions and returns query results; explicitly identifies SQL injection and database disclosure.

expectations.text: NoSQL injection in review update (operator/$where injection)
expectations.evidence: F15: routes/updateProductReviews.ts:16-19 uses untyped body id in a multi:true query; 'an operator-shaped ID can broaden the query'. Runtime operator support is appropriately qualified.

expectations.text: NoSQL injection in order tracking
expectations.evidence: F16: routes/trackOrder.ts:15-18 inserts a URL ID into a quoted $where JavaScript expression; predicate manipulation can select extra orders.

expectations.text: NoSQL $where sleep / injection in review listing
expectations.evidence: F16: routes/showProductReviews.ts:31-36 concatenates ID into $where and :17-25 installs blocking sleep; identifies predicate manipulation and CPU blocking.

expectations.text: SSTI / code execution via username rendered in pug template
expectations.evidence: F22: routes/userProfile.ts:57-65 extracts #{...} code from username, calls eval, and inserts result into Pug source before compilation at :90.

expectations.text: Sandboxed eval of B2B order payload (RCE / DoS)
expectations.evidence: F29: routes/b2bOrder.ts:18-32 evaluates caller code through notevil with a two-second timeout; repeated expensive expressions can block event loop. No unsupported sandbox escape claimed.

expectations.text: YAML parsing of uploads (yaml bomb)
expectations.evidence: F29: routes/fileUpload.ts:103-127 calls JSON.stringify(yaml.load(data)); explicitly identifies nested/aliased document expansion, memory and event-loop exhaustion.

expectations.text: XXE in XML upload (noent)
expectations.evidence: F26: routes/fileUpload.ts:77-83 sends uploaded XML to lib/xml.ts:19-35 with filesystem providers and NOENT/DTDLOAD; process-readable entity content can enter error response.

expectations.text: Zip slip in zip upload handling
expectations.evidence: F25: routes/fileUpload.ts:27-35 checks project-path substring then writes archive-controlled path under uploads/complaints; parent segments escape intended root.

expectations.text: Upload size/type enforced client-side or after processing
expectations.evidence: F28 identifies a different uploadToDisk memory-upload route lacking size limits. F45 cites fileUpload.ts:62-68 for arbitrary MIME labels in metrics, but does not identify complaint size/type validation as pass-through bookkeeping, the 100000-vs-200000 limit mismatch, or client-side-only enforcement. Correct general upload concerns are present, but the specified root cause is not established. Borderline broader-class interpretation recorded separately.

expectations.text: Mass assignment on user registration (role, etc.)
expectations.evidence: F10: server.ts registration does not allowlist fields, verify.ts:52-56 passes through, and models/user.ts:76-95 persists privileged roles; login signs supplied role.

expectations.text: Weak server-side registration validation (empty email/password, repeat check client-only)
expectations.evidence: F10 covers role mass assignment, not missing email/password validity or server-side repeat validation. No finding names empty registration or client-only password-repeat enforcement.

expectations.text: Negative quantity / price manipulation in basket & order
expectations.evidence: F31: basketItems.ts:87-101 checks only upper bounds; basketitem model lacks positive constraint; order.ts subtracts negative inventory quantities and multiplies them into price/wallet totals.

expectations.text: Deluxe membership payment bypass
expectations.evidence: F32: routes/deluxe.ts:24-40 tests only wallet/card strings; other paymentMode values fall through to role upgrade/token issuance.

expectations.text: Coupon codes forgeable (z85, no secret) / expiry not enforced
expectations.evidence: F30: lib/insecurity.ts:97-118 uses unsigned Z85 month/discount; coupon/order handlers apply it; alternative campaign trusts caller timestamp instead of server date.

expectations.text: Null byte / path filter bypass and directory listing on /ftp
expectations.evidence: F37: fileServer.ts checks suffix then truncates literal %00, allowing backup.ext%00.pdf to target backup.ext. F36 identifies public FTP directory index at server.ts:288-303.

expectations.text: Access logs served publicly
expectations.evidence: F08/F36: server.ts:301-303 publicly serves support logs; combined logging at :364 retains password-change URLs.

expectations.text: Admin area guarded only client-side / admin REST without role check
expectations.evidence: F11: frontend AdminGuard cannot protect HTTP; generated user listing and administrative operations use generic auth without roles.

expectations.text: Feedback CRUD without auth or ownership (delete any, forge UserId, zero stars, captcha reuse)
expectations.evidence: F11 identifies generic-auth Feedback DELETE without role restriction; F12 identifies body-controlled UserId on public Feedback POST; F38 identifies reusable exposed CAPTCHA answers. Zero-star case not discussed, but several mechanisms in this grouped root are established.

expectations.text: Basket read by ID without ownership check
expectations.evidence: F13: routes/basket.ts:18-19 reads URL ID after authentication without proving owner.

expectations.text: Basket item add with BasketId from body / duplicate key parsing
expectations.evidence: F14: utils.ts preserves duplicate keys; basketItems.ts authorizes first BasketId but persists last, permitting cross-user addition.

expectations.text: Product review author taken from body / update without author check
expectations.evidence: F15: createProductReviews.ts:23-28 stores body author; updateProductReviews.ts lacks author predicate, permitting cross-user edits.

expectations.text: Product PUT allowed for non-admin
expectations.evidence: F11 and API matrix: server.ts:391-394 has product PUT authorization commented out; anonymous product updates are explicitly identified.

expectations.text: CSRF on profile update (form POST accepted cross-origin, no token)
expectations.evidence: F24: updateUserProfile.ts cookie authentication, server.ts form-urlencoded support, absent CSRF/Origin rejection; qualifies modern SameSite restrictions.

expectations.text: SSRF via profile image URL fetch
expectations.evidence: F21: profileImageUrlUpload.ts:18-30 fetches arbitrary imageUrl without destination/redirect restrictions and saves response in public upload directory.

expectations.text: Weak / hard-coded seed credentials and test accounts
expectations.evidence: Seed-user datasets explicitly excluded; no weak/static seed or frontend test-account credential finding. F07 deterministic OAuth passwords is a different root cause.

expectations.text: Password reset by security question, no rate limit, guessable answers
expectations.evidence: F39: resetPassword.ts:35-46 relies on reusable knowledge answer; recovery-question enumeration and spoofable IP-based limiter described. It correctly acknowledges an IP limiter rather than literally claiming none; F36 additionally identifies exposed recovery-answer configuration.

expectations.text: OAuth login derives password from base64(reversed email) client-side
expectations.evidence: F07: oauth.component.ts:29-36 registers base64(reversed email) and :46-47 logs in with it; backend verifies no provider assertion.

expectations.text: Change password skips current-password check when param absent (GET params)
expectations.evidence: F08: changePassword.ts:39 checks current password only if supplied and reads credentials from GET query at :14-17.

expectations.text: TOTP secret stored in plaintext in users table
expectations.evidence: F09 identifies readable totpSecret in complete UserModel fields and responses/JWTs, states exposed seeds compromise second factor, and calls for protected TOTP storage. It does not use the word plaintext or separately identify the database write, but identifies unprotected model-held seeds and their disclosure. Source models/user.ts defines a plain STRING without encryption. Broad semantic match recorded as ambiguous. Coordinator adjudication: retain the conservative distinction between seed disclosure and an explicit plaintext-at-rest root cause, equally for both reports. Source knowledge supplied by the grader cannot fill that report omission.

expectations.text: Weak crypto: MD5 password hashing, hard-coded HMAC/RSA keys
expectations.evidence: F06: lib/insecurity.ts:41 plain unsalted MD5 and :42 shared source HMAC key. F03 identifies source-embedded RSA private signing key.

expectations.text: JWT: alg none / RSA public key confusion accepted, legacy express-jwt
expectations.evidence: F04 lists old JWT libraries and missing algorithm allowlist but explicitly says acceptance of none or RSA/HMAC confusion is 'not independently established'. Different token-purpose flaws and known private key do not establish this root.

expectations.text: Hard-coded encryption keys and key files shipped (encryptionkeys/, ctf.key, premium reward AES key)
expectations.evidence: F03 identifies hard-coded private key in lib/insecurity.ts and served Terraform; F36 identifies public encryptionkeys directory and key handlers. Source verification confirmed matching key material after normalizing source escapes. Specific premium/ctf keys not inspected; grouped root credit for exposed shipped key material.

expectations.text: Prometheus /metrics unauthenticated
expectations.evidence: F36 identifies anonymous /metrics at server.ts:696 and routes/metrics.ts, disclosing process and business metrics.

expectations.text: Verbose error handler / stack traces in responses
expectations.evidence: F36 identifies unconditional errorhandler() at server.ts:702 and developer details returned; formatting is explicitly dependency-qualified.

expectations.text: XSS sinks: search query via bypassSecurityTrustHtml, product description innerHTML, order-id reflection, True-Client-IP stored and rendered, outdated sanitize-html, video subtitle injection into pug, CSP header built from profile image URL
expectations.evidence: F18 traces search query and reflected orderId to bypassSecurityTrustHtml/innerHTML; F19 traces product/email/IP trust bypasses; F23 CSP interpolation; subtitle follow-up names raw VTT script injection. Sanitizer exploit is left unconfirmed. Multiple actual sinks satisfy this grouped root.

expectations.text: Open redirect allowlist uses substring match
expectations.evidence: No finding identifies isRedirectAllowed substring matching or open redirect. Reading redirect/security helpers in process/scope is not detection evidence.

expectations.text: JSONP whoami callback leaks email cross-origin
expectations.evidence: F24 identifies currentUser.ts:54-58 authenticated JSONP and cross-origin script reads when eligible cookies are sent; F09 describes unconstrained fields. Source confirms standard response includes email.

expectations.text: Known-vulnerable / typosquatted dependencies pinned in manifests
expectations.evidence: Additional observations explicitly leave dependency verification open and assert no vulnerability from version strings. No concrete vulnerable/typosquatted component finding is substantiated; outdated JWT pins alone do not establish this row.

grading_scope.method: Independent complete report/process reading, with targeted static source adjudication only. No counterpart, existing grading.json, historical results, live tests, or delegation. Source/report unchanged.
grading_scope.rules: 40 binary core rows; nine separate binary bonuses. Broad grouped rows receive credit for an evidenced submechanism, not mere file inventory.

ambiguities.reason: F28 has genuine missing upload limits but for memory uploads, while F45 refers to fileUpload.ts only for metrics MIME cardinality. Broad upload-class interpretation could award; strict complaint validation mechanism did not.

F09 evidences unprotected model-held TOTP seeds/disclosure, but not explicit storage-write analysis or the word plaintext. Credited semantic mechanism; stricter explicit storage requirement could reject.
Hard-coded signing material and public key directory covered; reward/ctf encryption specifics not. Rubric groups several secrets.
Wallet event attribution is different from contract/mint/sandbox mechanisms; broader NFT route interpretation could award.
IaC subcase detected through /infrastructure route, despite rubric description referring to client assets.
Same-origin active SVG publishing credited under 'or similar'; does not cover the precise delivery-address challenge.

false_positive_review.limits: No verified false claim was found in the selected checks; this is not a statement that every claim is true or that the report has zero false positives. Not all 48 findings or dependency/generated-API/browser behavior were independently verified. No runtime, provider/model, parser, concurrency, deployed-state, or contract behavior tested.
checks: F03: static key comparison initially required normalizing literal source escapes; underlying private-key base64 matches Terraform exactly. server.ts exposes infrastructure and only filters annotations; no values repeated.

F09: memory.ts joins UserModel without exclusion and serializes result; user model has no default secret scope and plain totpSecret field; server.ts public registration confirmed. Actual populated records not observed.
F17/B3: dataExport.ts masks email and selects orders with that lossy identity.
F21/B8: profileImageUrlUpload.ts accepts .svg, fetches arbitrary URL, and writes returned bytes into public upload location; browser execution remains conditional.
F24: currentUser.ts selects arbitrary fields and sends JSONP on callback; cross-site cookie eligibility remains conditional.
F27/B2: dataErasure.ts passes body/layout into res.render in gated and fallback branches; installed HBS resolution unverified.
F28: server.ts places uploadToDisk before authentication and disk Multer config has no size limit; actual exhaustion untested.
F33: wallet.ts increments balance from request after owned-card lookup only; payment integration absence confirmed within handler.
F40-F42: chat.ts decodes token without verification, compares masked emails, allows unrestricted numeric coupon tool, and streams tool-call input to all clients; model outcomes untested.
F43: request.interceptor.ts applies stored token/email without origin restriction; user.service.ts has external Google userinfo HttpClient request; actual CORS delivery unverified.

F47-F48: web3Wallet.ts inserts arbitrary request address in global Set before provider setup; nftMint.ts consumes global observed events by caller-supplied address. These support the report's bounded training-state/resource claims, not B5 contract weaknesses.

calibration.assessment: Strong source-versus-runtime qualification, explicit confidence labels, gate/platform conditions, attack prerequisites and bounded impacts. Report avoids equating CORS wildcard with credentialed access, known versions with proven CVEs, or template infrastructure with deployed infrastructure.
cautions: F03/F09 Critical ratings assume real users/data and exploit consequences; training adaptation context is stated.
F27 labels High potential impact/medium confidence and explains dependency/file-read limits; unresolved acceptance is not a confirmed false positive.
F04 leaves alg-none/confusion unconfirmed; that is a coverage miss rather than a false claim.

coverage_statement.evidence: Final 'Reviewed scope and explicit exclusions' plus process ledger distinguish full reads, focused ranges, search-only and inventory-only. Excludes seeds, contracts, dependency implementations, deployment/runtime and many assets.
areas_named_as_reviewed: lib/insecurity.ts, utils, XML and webhook helpers
selected frontend guards/services/templates and DOM sinks
coverage_statement.process_evidence_limit: Self-reported process log only; full execution transcript unavailable. Its claims of read operations, no runtime/external access, and 135 anchor checks are not independently proven by transcript.

execution_metrics.reason: No full transcript or token telemetry supplied; not inferred from report size.

suggestions.reason: Specify whether credit requires exact challenge mechanism/sink or a related vulnerability at an alternate sink. Broad grouped wording (especially 'or similar') permits materially different grades despite equivalent evidence.
Multiple independent mechanisms share one binary row; one sink passes despite omitted variants. Preserve frozen score now, but future coverage reporting should separate submechanisms.

eval_feedback.overall: Rubric is usable but combines exact-root and broad-family rows. Explicit ambiguities are preserved for coordinator adjudication without consulting other grades.

bonus.text: Race condition on review likes (routes/likeProductReviews.ts) — timingAttack
bonus.evidence: F35: likeProductReviews.ts checks likedBy, increments count, waits 150ms, then writes voter array; parallel requests can repeat increment.

bonus.text: Local file read in data erasure layout param (routes/dataErasure.ts) — lfr
bonus.evidence: F27: dataErasure.ts spreads caller body/layout into res.render, with a weak denylist; identifies local-file/template disclosure and 100-character gate limit. Source verifies both branches forward body.

bonus.text: Data export matching other users' data (routes/dataExport.ts) — dataExport
bonus.evidence: F17: dataExport.ts:21-33 selects orders by vowel-masked email, allowing distinct valid emails to collide. Source verifies matching query.

bonus.text: Chatbot prompt injection / debug info to non-admins (routes/chat.ts) — chatbotPromptInjection, chatbotGreedyInjection, aiDebugging, systemPromptExtraction
bonus.evidence: F41 identifies untrusted prompt/history and no server enforcement for coupon policy; F42 identifies tool-call traces streamed regardless of admin status. Source confirms tool schema and unconditional trace output. Successful model jailbreak not claimed.

bonus.text: Web3: reentrancy in wallet contract, NFT mint logic, sandbox route (routes/web3Wallet.ts, routes/nftMint.ts, data/static/web3-snippets) — web3Wallet, nftMint, web3Sandbox
bonus.evidence: F47/F48 concern forged attribution of observed events and unbounded listener registration, not contract reentrancy, NFT mint authorization logic, or sandbox-route weakness. Contract implementations explicitly excluded. Broader interpretation of NFT logic is ambiguous but not credited.

bonus.text: Hidden routes reachable client-side (token sale, score board, privacy policy, IaC files under assets, extra language file, blueprint under public assets) — tokenSale, scoreBoard, misplacedIacFiles, extraLanguage, retrieveBlueprint
bonus.evidence: F03 identifies anonymous infrastructure-file route server.ts:268-285 serving Terraform including key material. Credits the IaC-file exposure subcase; other listed hidden routes are not detected. Current source serves /infrastructure rather than assets.
Progress/restoration route bodies excluded and no Hashids/continue-code forgery finding.

bonus.text: SVG/HTML injection into delivery address or similar — svgInjection
bonus.evidence: F21 explicitly identifies allowed .svg server fetch, publication under shop origin, and active SVG execution when opened as a document. Source confirms .svg allowance and public saved path. Credited under 'or similar'; no delivery-address injection is identified and strict challenge-specific interpretation could reject this match. Coordinator adjudication: credit the genuine active-SVG publication mechanism under the rubric's explicit "or similar" wording, equally for both reports. This does not credit the specific delivery-address challenge.

bonus.text: Missing output encoding of image filename — missingEncoding
bonus.evidence: No image-filename output-encoding finding. Filename sanitization or upload MIME concerns do not identify this class.

adjudication.method: Coordinator reconciled independent grades after both were saved. Raw independent grades are retained in grading-independent.json; initial baseline coordinator grade is also retained.
adjudication.G11: No credit in either report: the unbounded memory upload and metrics MIME-label issue are not the complaint-upload validation bypass.
adjudication.G31: No credit in either report for storage: usable-seed disclosure is established, but explicit plaintext-at-rest root cause is absent. Broader matching would add one core point to both.
adjudication.B6: Credit both for the public IaC-file subcase explicitly included in the bonus; no credit inferred for hidden frontend routes. This corrects the initial baseline coordinator exclusion.
adjudication.B8: Credit both for actual same-origin active-SVG publication under "or similar". Narrow delivery-address-only interpretation would subtract one bonus point from both.
adjudication.effect: Adjudication applies identical rules; core difference remains two points and bonus scores are tied.
